timing_definitions.total_elapsed_ns: client monotonic interval starts immediately before sending the start control and ends after the final message check and release; setup, corpus preparation, TLS upgrade, warmup, and close are outside
timing_definitions.receive_assembly_ns: sum of intervals around each WebSocket receive API call; Bend includes result unwrapping, and both include blocking, TLS/socket work, parser/reassembly, and any library assembly/copy
timing_definitions.validation_release_ns: sum of opcode validation, ordered expected-byte equality over the full message, and immediate release of actual and expected buffers; the 8-byte decimal sequence prefix is part of exact equality
timing_definitions.residual_ns: total minus receive/assembly and validation/release; includes start-control send, loop/control work, and gaps between phase samples; not pure overhead or network time
timing_definitions.control_mode: same client validation/release code and common total timer, but no per-message phase clock calls
timing_definitions.observer_effect: paired phase/control total differences estimate the additional per-message phase clock calls within this diagnostic client skeleton, not against the historical client
timing_definitions.peer_send_interval: peer monotonic interval starts after decoding the start control and ends after the final TLS plaintext Write; client total includes sending the start control, so these intervals are not aligned or additive
timing_definitions.peer_tls_write_wall: sum of wall intervals around TLS Conn.Write calls; includes TLS work, blocking, and scheduling, and does not measure wire bytes
timing_definitions.peer_process_cpu: whole peer-process user/system CPU deltas sampled around the peer send interval; not thread-only CPU
timing_definitions.peer_observer_effect: peer timing instrumentation is held constant in all four client conditions; its observer effect is not separately isolated

corpus.messages: ordered binary messages of exactly 65,536 bytes
corpus.warmup: one binary warmup echo, exact byte and opcode checked before total timer

negative_controls: corrupt final byte in first payload and swap sequence messages 1 and 2; both clients must reject for both flush batches
